# Decisions: auto-update

- 2026-08-05T09:27:36.783Z — chose **D1: Auto-update means a cached version check that only ever TELLS you. A detached child refreshes ~/.local/state/sofar/update.json (24h TTL, XDG_STATE_HOME honored); every foreground surface only READS that file, so no command ever waits on the network. The parent claims the slot (writes checked_at before spawning) so the statusline, which renders every prompt, cannot start a thundering herd. Surfaced on the statusline (cyan info segment, color law) and on status/init/doctor as a trailing line. Checks run ONLY when planUpgrade() resolves global-npm, and never under CI or SOFAR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK. True auto-install exists but is opt-in (`sofar upgrade --auto on`, ~/.config/sofar/config.json) and is pitched only in runUpgrade's success message, at the moment the chore was just felt.** over Installing updates silently by default; a synchronous `npm view` on the statusline or SessionStart hot path; a new doctor AXIS, which would turn doctor's exit code non-zero merely because a release landed; nagging source checkouts, local deps and npx runs, which either cannot self-upgrade or are already latest; and printing the --auto pitch before --auto exists. because `sofar upgrade` already solves installing correctly (it derives the real npm prefix from the running binary). What it cannot do is tell you an update exists — that is the whole gap. Notification is safe; unattended installation is not symmetric with it, because upgrading replaces the binary AND leaves repo wiring stale (runUpgrade's own success message says to re-run `sofar init` for hook shims and the protocol block), so the install must stay a thing the user chose. The read/refresh split is what makes the hint free: reading a JSON file is sub-millisecond, and the statusline path renders on every prompt. Gating on global-npm kills dev-noise in this very repo, where a source checkout would otherwise nag on every render.
